<a id="exoplanets-host-systems"></a>
### Exoplanet host systems (one record per host star) derived from the PSCompPars snapshot

- **Dataset id:** `exoplanets-host-systems`
- **Organization:** Derived by the Cosmos/AstroNexus project from NASA Exoplanet Archive data (Caltech/IPAC)
- **Version:** derived from the PSCompPars snapshot retrieved 2026-10-16T18:28:50.774Z
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-16T18:28:50.774Z
- **License:** No explicit licence is published by the NASA Exoplanet Archive. The data are publicly and freely accessible (NASA-funded archive operated by Caltech/IPAC); the archive requests its standard acknowledgement, citation of Christiansen et al. (2025) and the table DOIs, and credit to the original literature references (linked per parameter in references.json). No redistribution restriction is documented; this snapshot is redistributed unmodified in value for non-commercial educational display with full attribution. (<https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/acknowledge.html>)
- **Provenance class:** derived
- **Endpoint:** <https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/TAP/sync>
- **Update cadence:** Regenerated whenever planets.json is rebuilt
- **Rate limits:** Not documented by the archive (TAP documentation states no limit). This pipeline makes 8 TAP sync requests per refresh, >= 1.5 s apart, with User-Agent identification.
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Place exoplanet host stars in the 3D star field (ICRS Cartesian parsecs), host-level stellar parameters for system views and the habitability lab, and the index of each host's planets in planets.json.

**Mechanism.** Offline aggregation of the PSCompPars snapshot by hostname + spherical-to-Cartesian conversion (x = d cos(dec) cos(ra), y = d cos(dec) sin(ra), z = d sin(dec))

**Query.**

```
select pl_name,pl_letter,hostname,sy_snum,sy_pnum,sy_mnum,cb_flag,pl_controv_flag,discoverymethod,disc_year,disc_facility,disc_refname,pl_orbper,pl_orbpererr1,pl_orbpererr2,pl_orbperlim,pl_orbper_reflink,pl_orbsmax,pl_orbsmaxerr1,pl_orbsmaxerr2,pl_orbsmaxlim,pl_orbsmax_reflink,pl_orbeccen,pl_orbeccenerr1,pl_orbeccenerr2,pl_orbeccenlim,pl_orbeccen_reflink,pl_orbincl,pl_orbinclerr1,pl_orbinclerr2,pl_orbincllim,pl_orbincl_reflink,pl_orblper,pl_orblpererr1,pl_orblpererr2,pl_orblperlim,pl_orblper_reflink,pl_tranmid,pl_tranmiderr1,pl_tranmiderr2,pl_tranmidlim,pl_tranmid_reflink,pl_rade,pl_radeerr1,pl_radeerr2,pl_radelim,pl_rade_reflink,pl_bmasse,pl_bmasseerr1,pl_bmasseerr2,pl_bmasselim,pl_bmasse_reflink,pl_dens,pl_denserr1,pl_denserr2,pl_denslim,pl_dens_reflink,pl_insol,pl_insolerr1,pl_insolerr2,pl_insollim,pl_insol_reflink,pl_eqt,pl_eqterr1,pl_eqterr2,pl_eqtlim,pl_eqt_reflink,st_teff,st_tefferr1,st_tefferr2,st_tefflim,st_teff_reflink,st_rad,st_raderr1,st_raderr2,st_radlim,st_rad_reflink,st_mass,st_masserr1,st_masserr2,st_masslim,st_mass_reflink,st_lum,st_lumerr1,st_lumerr2,st_lumlim,st_lum_reflink,st_met,st_meterr1,st_meterr2,st_metlim,st_met_reflink,st_age,st_ageerr1,st_ageerr2,st_agelim,st_age_reflink,st_logg,st_loggerr1,st_loggerr2,st_logglim,st_logg_reflink,sy_dist,sy_disterr1,sy_disterr2,sy_dist_reflink,sy_plx,sy_plxerr1,sy_plxerr2,sy_plx_reflink,sy_vmag,sy_vmagerr1,sy_vmagerr2,sy_vmag_reflink,sy_kmag,sy_kmagerr1,sy_kmagerr2,sy_kmag_reflink,sy_gaiamag,sy_gaiamagerr1,sy_gaiamagerr2,sy_gaiamag_reflink,pl_tranmid_systemref,pl_bmassprov,st_spectype,st_spectype_reflink,st_metratio,ra,dec,ra_reflink,sy_pmra,sy_pmraerr1,sy_pmraerr2,sy_pmdec,sy_pmdecerr1,sy_pmdecerr2,sy_pm,sy_pm_reflink,hd_name,hip_name,tic_id,gaia_dr3_id,pl_radj,pl_bmassj from pscomppars
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/exoplanets/build.mjs

**Fallback.** If systems.json is missing: hosts can be rebuilt client-side by grouping planets.json rows on hostname and converting ra/dec/sy_dist; if both files are missing hide the exoplanet layer.

**Limitations.** xPc/yPc/zPc are derived (not observed) and inherit the archive distance uncertainties; 28 hosts have no distance (null coordinates). Host stellar values follow a documented selection rule because composite rows of the same host can disagree (222 hosts; listed per host in stVarying). Positions are at the source epoch (posEpochJyr), not propagated. Distances for microlensing hosts are model-dependent with large uncertainties.

**Citation.** This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under the Exoplanet Exploration Program. <a id="exoplanets-pscomppars"></a>
### NASA Exoplanet Archive: Planetary Systems Composite Parameters (PSCompPars), all confirmed planets, with default-parameter-set provenance from the Planetary Systems (PS) table

- **Dataset id:** `exoplanets-pscomppars`
- **Organization:** NASA Exoplanet Archive, operated by Caltech/IPAC (NExScI) for the NASA Exoplanet Exploration Program
- **Version:** live archive state at retrieval (latest PS default-row release date 2026-10-15; 6451 confirmed planets = count(*) from ps where default_flag=1)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-16T18:28:50.774Z
- **License:** No explicit licence is published by the NASA Exoplanet Archive. The data are publicly and freely accessible (NASA-funded archive operated by Caltech/IPAC); the archive requests its standard acknowledgement, citation of Christiansen et al. (2025) and the table DOIs, and credit to the original literature references (linked per parameter in references.json). No redistribution restriction is documented; this snapshot is redistributed unmodified in value for non-commercial educational display with full attribution. (<https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/acknowledge.html>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/TAP/sync>
- **Update cadence:** Archive is updated weekly (Thursday news/update cycle); this snapshot is refreshed on demand with `node scripts/data/exoplanets/run.mjs --refresh`
- **Rate limits:** Not documented by the archive (TAP documentation states no limit). This pipeline makes 8 TAP sync requests per refresh, >= 1.5 s apart, with User-Agent identification.
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Exoplanet layer, planet/system info panels and habitability-lab inputs: one row per confirmed planet with orbit, radius, mass, density, insolation, equilibrium temperature, host-star parameters, discovery data, uncertainties, limit flags and per-parameter literature references.

**Mechanism.** IVOA TAP sync, ADQL -> JSON (format=json); raw responses cached gzip-compressed in data-raw/exoplanets; normalised to compact {fields, rows} JSON

**Query.**

```
select pl_name,pl_letter,hostname,sy_snum,sy_pnum,sy_mnum,cb_flag,pl_controv_flag,discoverymethod,disc_year,disc_facility,disc_refname,pl_orbper,pl_orbpererr1,pl_orbpererr2,pl_orbperlim,pl_orbper_reflink,pl_orbsmax,pl_orbsmaxerr1,pl_orbsmaxerr2,pl_orbsmaxlim,pl_orbsmax_reflink,pl_orbeccen,pl_orbeccenerr1,pl_orbeccenerr2,pl_orbeccenlim,pl_orbeccen_reflink,pl_orbincl,pl_orbinclerr1,pl_orbinclerr2,pl_orbincllim,pl_orbincl_reflink,pl_orblper,pl_orblpererr1,pl_orblpererr2,pl_orblperlim,pl_orblper_reflink,pl_tranmid,pl_tranmiderr1,pl_tranmiderr2,pl_tranmidlim,pl_tranmid_reflink,pl_rade,pl_radeerr1,pl_radeerr2,pl_radelim,pl_rade_reflink,pl_bmasse,pl_bmasseerr1,pl_bmasseerr2,pl_bmasselim,pl_bmasse_reflink,pl_dens,pl_denserr1,pl_denserr2,pl_denslim,pl_dens_reflink,pl_insol,pl_insolerr1,pl_insolerr2,pl_insollim,pl_insol_reflink,pl_eqt,pl_eqterr1,pl_eqterr2,pl_eqtlim,pl_eqt_reflink,st_teff,st_tefferr1,st_tefferr2,st_tefflim,st_teff_reflink,st_rad,st_raderr1,st_raderr2,st_radlim,st_rad_reflink,st_mass,st_masserr1,st_masserr2,st_masslim,st_mass_reflink,st_lum,st_lumerr1,st_lumerr2,st_lumlim,st_lum_reflink,st_met,st_meterr1,st_meterr2,st_metlim,st_met_reflink,st_age,st_ageerr1,st_ageerr2,st_agelim,st_age_reflink,st_logg,st_loggerr1,st_loggerr2,st_logglim,st_logg_reflink,sy_dist,sy_disterr1,sy_disterr2,sy_dist_reflink,sy_plx,sy_plxerr1,sy_plxerr2,sy_plx_reflink,sy_vmag,sy_vmagerr1,sy_vmagerr2,sy_vmag_reflink,sy_kmag,sy_kmagerr1,sy_kmagerr2,sy_kmag_reflink,sy_gaiamag,sy_gaiamagerr1,sy_gaiamagerr2,sy_gaiamag_reflink,pl_tranmid_systemref,pl_bmassprov,st_spectype,st_spectype_reflink,st_metratio,ra,dec,ra_reflink,sy_pmra,sy_pmraerr1,sy_pmraerr2,sy_pmdec,sy_pmdecerr1,sy_pmdecerr2,sy_pm,sy_pm_reflink,hd_name,hip_name,tic_id,gaia_dr3_id,pl_radj,pl_bmassj from pscomppars ;; select pl_name,hostname,default_flag,soltype,pl_refname,st_refname,sy_refname,pl_pubdate,releasedate,rowupdate from ps where default_flag=1 ;; select count(*) as n from ps where default_flag=1
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/exoplanets/build.mjs

**Fallback.** If planets.json is missing or invalid: hide the exoplanet layer and catalogue presets of the habitability lab and show "exoplanet catalogue unavailable"; the lab may still run on user-entered parameters labelled illustrative. Never substitute invented values.

**Limitations.** Composite table: a planet's parameters may come from different references and need not be self-consistent (use the PS table for a single consistent solution). pl_eqt assumptions (Bond albedo, heat redistribution) differ by reference: 1090 values were calculated by the archive (zero albedo, full redistribution, no uncertainties), others come from papers or catalogues such as the Kepler DR25 KOI table. 3035 masses (pl_bmassprov = 'M-R relationship') are archive estimates from the Chen & Kipping (2017) mass-radius relation, not measurements; pl_bmasse may be a minimum mass (Msini). Archive-calculated values carry no uncertainties. Positions are ICRS at the source epoch (J2015.5 for TIC v8), not propagated. pl_tranmid time standards vary (see pl_tranmid_systemref). Limit-flag semantics (1 = upper limit, -1 = lower limit) were verified empirically (archive docs do not state them); one row carries an undocumented pl_denslim value of 9.

**Citation.** This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under the Exoplanet Exploration Program. Please cite Christiansen, J. L., et al. 2025, "The NASA Exoplanet Archive and Exoplanet Follow-up Observing Program: Data, Tools, and Usage", Planetary Science Journal, 6, 186, doi:10.3847/PSJ/ade3c2; PSCompPars doi:10.26133/NEA13; PS doi:10.26133/NEA12; and credit the original literature references listed in references.json.

## Domain: orbital

<a id="celestrak-gp-omm"></a>
### CelesTrak GP mean element sets (CCSDS OMM keywords, CSV): published groups, special data sets and NAME searches

- **Dataset id:** `celestrak-gp-omm`
- **Organization:** CelesTrak (T.S. Kelso); data from U.S. Space Force 18th/19th Space Defense Squadrons via Space-Track.org
- **Version:** live archive state at retrieval (GP downloads 2026-10-16T18:29:34.217Z .. 2026-10-17T06:50:38.227Z; CelesTrak GP update cycle current as of 2026-10-16 18:05:42 UTC)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-17T06:50:38.227Z
- **License:** No formal open-data licence. CelesTrak makes the data freely available to all users subject to its usage policy (https://celestrak.org/usage-policy.php). The GP/OMM element sets and SATCAT are "basic SSA data" originating from USSPACECOM (U.S. Space Force 18th/19th Space Defense Squadrons) via Space-Track.org, for which USSPACECOM grants "express blanket approval for transfer/redistribution of basic SSA data ... conditioned on appropriate citation" (Space-Track User Agreement, section "Redistribution of Basic SSA Information"). (<https://celestrak.org/usage-policy.php>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/gp.php>
- **Update cadence:** Upstream refresh every 2 h. Cosmos snapshot refreshed manually: node scripts/data/orbital/fetch.mjs --refresh && node scripts/data/orbital/build.mjs (never more than once per upstream update).
- **Rate limits:** CelesTrak usage policy (2026-05-22): download each data set at most once per update (GP every 2 h, SupGP 2 h, SATCAT 1-2x per day); since 2026-03-26 a repeat request for GP Active/Starlink before the next update returns HTTP 403; stop querying on any non-200 (301/403/404/5xx); >50 HTTP errors in 2 h or >100 MB/day may get the IP firewalled; directory/query pages at most once per hour. No per-second limit documented (this pipeline waits 2.5 s between requests).
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** SGP4 mean elements for every tracked on-orbit object rendered and propagated in the Earth orbital-environment layer; CelesTrak group memberships for filters (stations, constellations, GNSS, GEO, debris clouds, ...).

**Mechanism.** HTTPS GET gp.php?{GROUP|SPECIAL|NAME}=...&FORMAT=CSV (OMM keywords, 9-digit-safe) -> merged by NORAD_CAT_ID (latest EPOCH wins, group tags unioned) -> catalog.json rows with elementSource="celestrak-gp".

**Query.**

```
GROUP={active,fengyun-1c-debris,cosmos-2251-debris,iridium-33-debris,analyst,last-30-days,stations,visual,weather,resource,sar,sarsat,dmc,tdrss,argos,planet,spire,geo,intelsat,ses,eutelsat,telesat,oneweb,qianfan,hulianwang,kuiper,iridium-NEXT,orbcomm,globalstar,amateur,satnogs,x-comm,other-comm,gnss,gps-ops,glo-ops,galileo,beidou,sbas,science,geodetic,engineering,education,military,radar,cubesat}&FORMAT=CSV (46 requests); SPECIAL={GPZ,GPZ-PLUS,DECAYING}&FORMAT=CSV; NAME=DEB&FORMAT=CSV; NAME=R/B&FORMAT=CSV. Starlink group intentionally not downloaded (subset of active per CelesTrak).
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/orbital/build.mjs

**Fallback.** If catalog.json is missing or fails to parse, hide the orbital-object layer and show "orbital catalog unavailable" (never synthesize objects). Per object: hasElements=false -> render from SATCAT shape with illustrative phase and label it reconstructed; elementSource=null -> list only, do not render.

**Limitations.** GP elements are SGP4 mean elements (TEME, UTC epochs) with ~1 km accuracy at epoch degrading by km/day; ages differ per object (median 1.14 d at retrieval). 3813 of 35652 on-orbit objects have no public GP in the downloaded sets (no group covers inactive payloads; ~800 objects are NEA "no elements available", e.g. classified; others have no current GP at CelesTrak) and fall back to SATCAT shape. 594 analyst objects (uncorrelated tracks, numbers 8xxxx / 2xxxxx) are included as class "unknown". The tracked catalogue (~10 cm LEO / ~1 m GEO detection limits) is a small fraction of the real debris population (ESA MASTER-8: ~1.5 million objects 1-10 cm).

**Citation.** Orbital data: CelesTrak (Dr T.S. Kelso, https://celestrak.org) - GP element sets and SATCAT; source data: U.S. Space Force 18th & 19th Space Defense Squadrons / USSPACECOM via Space-Track.org.

**Fields used (15).** `OBJECT_NAME`, `OBJECT_ID`, `EPOCH`, `MEAN_MOTION`, `ECCENTRICITY`, `INCLINATION`, `RA_OF_ASC_NODE`, `ARG_OF_PERICENTER`, `MEAN_ANOMALY`, `NORAD_CAT_ID`, `BSTAR`, `MEAN_MOTION_DOT`, `MEAN_MOTION_DDOT`, `EPHEMERIS_TYPE`, `CLASSIFICATION_TYPE`

**Files.**

- `public/data/orbital/catalog.json` (8.68 MB, 35,652 records)

<a id="celestrak-satcat"></a>
### CelesTrak Satellite Catalog (SATCAT), full CSV

- **Dataset id:** `celestrak-satcat`
- **Organization:** CelesTrak (T.S. Kelso); catalog maintained by U.S. Space Force 18th SDS, with CelesTrak corrections
- **Version:** SATCAT file Last-Modified 2026-10-15T20:56:28.000Z (71073 records incl. decayed; official catalog then at 101074)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-16T18:29:27.616Z
- **License:** No formal open-data licence. CelesTrak makes the data freely available to all users subject to its usage policy (https://celestrak.org/usage-policy.php). The GP/OMM element sets and SATCAT are "basic SSA data" originating from USSPACECOM (U.S. Space Force 18th/19th Space Defense Squadrons) via Space-Track.org, for which USSPACECOM grants "express blanket approval for transfer/redistribution of basic SSA data ... conditioned on appropriate citation" (Space-Track User Agreement, section "Redistribution of Basic SSA Information"). (<https://celestrak.org/usage-policy.php>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://celestrak.org/pub/satcat.csv>
- **Update cadence:** Upstream updated manually 1-2x per day; Cosmos snapshot refreshed manually with the GP data.
- **Rate limits:** CelesTrak usage policy (2026-05-22): download each data set at most once per update (GP every 2 h, SupGP 2 h, SATCAT 1-2x per day); since 2026-03-26 a repeat request for GP Active/Starlink before the next update returns HTTP 403; stop querying on any non-200 (301/403/404/5xx); >50 HTTP errors in 2 h or >100 MB/day may get the IP firewalled; directory/query pages at most once per hour. No per-second limit documented (this pipeline waits 2.5 s between requests).
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Authoritative list of on-orbit objects (no decay date, Earth-centred): object class, owner, launch date/site, RCS, operational status, docking; orbit shape (apogee/perigee/inclination/period) for objects without GP elements; population statistics by class/regime/altitude shell.

**Mechanism.** HTTPS GET of the static full-catalog CSV -> filter DECAY_DATE empty and ORBIT_CENTER = EA (or docked to an Earth-orbiting host) -> joined with GP by NORAD_CAT_ID.

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/orbital/build.mjs

**Fallback.** Without SATCAT the app cannot show owner/class/launch metadata; render GP objects with class from name heuristics only and flag metadata as unavailable.

**Limitations.** SATCAT apogee/perigee/period/inclination are rounded (km, 0.01 deg/min) and can be stale for objects without current elements. RCS (m^2) is missing for ~58% of on-orbit objects (rcsSize null). OWNER is the SATCAT source code (country/organisation), not necessarily the operator. Analyst objects are not in SATCAT.

**Citation.** Orbital data: CelesTrak (Dr T.S. Kelso, https://celestrak.org) - GP element sets and SATCAT; source data: U.S. Space Force 18th & 19th Space Defense Squadrons / USSPACECOM via Space-Track.org.

**Fields used (17).** `OBJECT_NAME`, `OBJECT_ID`, `NORAD_CAT_ID`, `OBJECT_TYPE`, `OPS_STATUS_CODE`, `OWNER`, `LAUNCH_DATE`, `LAUNCH_SITE`, `DECAY_DATE`, `PERIOD`, `INCLINATION`, `APOGEE`, `PERIGEE`, `RCS`, `DATA_STATUS_CODE`, `ORBIT_CENTER`, `ORBIT_TYPE`

**Files.**

- `public/data/orbital/catalog.json` (8.68 MB, 35,652 records)
- `public/data/orbital/summary.json` (18.5 KB)

**Purpose.** Kessler / debris laboratory: real-catalog shell populations and spatial densities; HUD counts; notable-object shortcuts.

**Mechanism.** Computed locally by build.mjs from the catalog rows (no separate download): regime classification, mean-altitude histogram, residence-time-weighted shell occupancy and spatial density; external reference figures (ESA, CelesTrak boxscore) quoted for context.

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/orbital/build.mjs

**Fallback.** If summary.json is missing, the app may recompute counts from catalog.json; hide shell-density charts otherwise.

**Limitations.** Shell statistics use mean (not osculating) apsides and a two-body residence-time model; satcat-shape rows use rounded SATCAT apsides. Only the tracked public catalogue is counted (objects >~10 cm in LEO); real densities including untracked debris are far higher.

**Citation.** Orbital data: CelesTrak (Dr T.S. Kelso, https://celestrak.org) - GP element sets and SATCAT; source data: U.S. Space Force 18th & 19th Space Defense Squadrons / USSPACECOM via Space-Track.org. Statistics computed by the Cosmos/AstroNexus project. Context figures: ESA Space Debris Office (sdup.esoc.esa.int/discosweb/statistics, 2026-10-14) and CelesTrak SATCAT boxscore (2026-10-15).

date-min=2026-10-16&date-max=2036-10-16&dist-max=0.05&body=Earth&sort=date&diameter=true&fullname=true ; plus des=99942&date-min=2029-01-01&date-max=2029-12-31&dist-max=0.05&body=Earth&diameter=true&fullname=true

**Limitations.** Predicted approaches change as orbits are refined; poorly observed objects have large distMin/distMax spread; diameter is measured only for a minority, otherwise null (H-based estimates are in neos.json).
